what: A static delivery 200, where the headers are the contract rather than the body: Content-Length, Accept-Ranges, Content-Range and Content-Type (010 spec 3.2). Three header values differ on every response ever taken from the two servers, and the pair carries all three - the response clock and X-Response-Time-ms, which behaviours 1.9 records and spec 3.3 excuses, and Server, which behaviours 4.1 records as a measured divergence, Atrium/<version> against the reference's Kestrel, and which spec 3.3 does NOT carry a row for. Accept-Ranges is spelled in different cases on the two sides on purpose: HTTP says header names are case-insensitive and the two servers are different stacks, so an engine that matched them by their bytes would report a finding about nothing on every delivery route.
